reason: R1 is a simple load-to-ground on the output; removing it typically does not break the PMOS bias/load structure, but it changes the DC operating point and output loading (VOUT1 may float higher). Caveat: if R1 was the only defined discharge path or load setting gain/swing, you may need another load or the output can become poorly defined.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (mainly affects DC level, loading, and gain; topology still operates)

reason: M9 appears to be a bias/helper device creating or modulating the internal node net4; removing it can still leave the main pull-up device (M7) present, but net4 may lose its intended biasing/drive. Caveat: without M9 (or another bias source), net4 may float and M7’s source/drain bias conditions may shift, so you may need to tie net4 to a fixed bias or otherwise define it.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (biasing robustness decreases; may require a replacement bias for net4)

reason: If you only care about preserving the bias node behavior at net4 (and not producing a valid VOUT1 output), M7 can be removed since it is the device that actually connects the internal node net4 to the output. Caveat: removing M7 eliminates the output pull-up path, so VOUT1 will be set only by whatever external load you attach (or it may float).
impact_estimate: Low only if VOUT1 output is not required; high if VOUT1 must be a defined output
